rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for something vanishing or a person going missing.

example.jyutping: ngo5 go3 ngan4 baau1 hou2 ci5 m4 gin3 zo2

rows.note: Choose this for a more formal or abstract statement that something has vanished; for an ordinary missing person, 唔見 or 失蹤 is more natural.

example.english: I watched the rumours slowly disappear.
example.traditional: 我睇住啲謠言慢慢消失。
example.jyutping: ngo5 tai2 zyu6 di1 jiu4 jin4 maan6 maan6 siu1 sat1

rows.note: Use this specifically when a person is missing, especially in the sense of being reported or treated as a missing person.

example.english: The police said that man did disappear.
example.traditional: 警方話嗰個男子失蹤咗。
example.jyutping: ging2 fong1 waa6 go2 go3 naam4 zi2 sat1 zung1 zo2

rows.note: Use this causative construction when someone deliberately makes another person disappear, including as a euphemism for abduction or political killing.

example.traditional: 有啲政客會令異見人士消失。
example.jyutping: jau5 di1 zing3 haak3 wui5 ling6 ji6 gin3 jan4 si6 siu1 sat1
